title: Elevated session protections and audit integration review for admin surfaces
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Scope: Harden RBAC v2 admin surfaces by introducing time-limited elevation tokens, SAML assertion validation hardening, and a tamper-evident audit pipeline. This ticket consolidates the outcomes of the Feb security review, the external pen-test report (red-team engagement 2026-02), and the threat modeling session on 2026-02-20.

Goals:
- Prevent indefinite or silently prolonged elevated sessions for admin/private APIs.
- Ensure SSO/SAML login flows include assertion replay protection and strict audience/recipient checks.
- Extend audit logging schema to include HMAC chain IDs, request origin metadata, and pre/post-elevation snapshots.
- Create automated validation tests and an observability dashboard for elevation usage and suspicious patterns.

Deliverables:
1) Implementation of short-lived elevation tokens (default TTL 5 minutes) with explicit re-auth (MFA) hooks for critical admin actions.
2) SAML verification library updates to enforce strict time-skew windows, nonce usage, and certificate rotation checks documented in the Confluence guidance.
3) Audit pipeline changes: append-only storage markers, per-event HMAC, and a small lambda to index elevation events for quick triage.
4) Remediation PRs for issues found in the pen-test with evidence and regression tests.

Out of scope: Full RBAC policy redesign (will be tracked in a follow-up EPIC), UI polish for non-admin flows.
threat_model_summary: Primary threats: privilege escalation via long-lived elevated tokens, SAML assertion replay or misrouting, lack of contextual audit (can't tie elevated action to pre-elevation state), and audit tampering. Mitigations include reducing token lifetime, adding MFA/consent on elevation, stronger SAML validation, and tamper-evident audit chaining.
acceptance_criteria: All admin elevation paths issue short-lived tokens (<=5m) and require MFA when configured
SAML verification layer fails intentionally malformed assertions and logs rejection reasons
Audit records for elevation events include pre/post state snapshot references and HMAC chain ID
Unit and integration tests cover replay attempts, expired tokens, and audit verification
Observability dashboard shows elevation rate, failures, and alerts on anomalous spikes

next_steps: 1) Complete CLI server-side enforcement test matrix and flip feature flag in staging. 2) Run full regression pen-test scope (replay, rotation, chain verification). 3) Schedule security review meeting (target 2026-03-20) for formal signoff. 4) Prepare customer security bulletin and internal runbook for incident response.
notes_on_performance: Initial staging benchmarks show <3% 99th token latency increase for admin flows after audit HMAC enrichment. We will monitor storage costs for indexer; bucketed retention policy recommended.
remediation_summary: Pen-test identified three actionable items: (a) long-lived elevation tokens — addressed by TTL+MFA; (b) SAML recipient/time-skew weaknesses — patched in SAML library and configuration; (c) audit gaps allowing weak correlation between pre/post state — addressed by adding snapshot references and HMAC chain IDs. Each fix includes regression tests and a follow-up verification by the external tester.
owner_notes: If customer_impact becomes high during staging we will pause rollout and open a customer advisory. Coordinate with SOC on key rotations before prod enabling.
